content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart’s Zagreb-Jarun store. I have nine years of experience in butcher shops and meat counters, completed vocational butcher training, and hold a HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate.

In my current role at Mesnica Kod Ante, I break down beef, pork and lamb, bone and trim cuts, and portion meat for the counter. I also make fresh sausages, rotate cold-room stock using FIFO, and record temperature checks twice daily. At the Dolac market stall, I served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till, and maintained clean, sanitised equipment. I enjoy advising customers on cuts and cooking, and would bring that practical, friendly service to FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” approach.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my butchery experience, attention to hygiene and reliability to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing my experience with you.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a concise, professional cover letter with a clear opening, relevant evidence, and an appropriate closing. It directly connects the candidate’s nine years of butchery experience, completed training, HACCP certification, meat preparation, customer service, till operation, and cleaning responsibilities to the advertised role. The examples are credible and supported by the original candidate information. The letter is slightly less impactful than it could be because it omits the candidate’s FIFO stock rotation and twice-daily temperature-recording detail, both of which closely match the job duties.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses a conventional structure, plain text headings are unnecessary for a short letter, and the content contains relevant terms including butcher, meat counter, vocational butcher training, HACCP, beef, pork, lamb, fresh sausages, FIFO, temperature checks, customer service, till, and sanitised equipment. The likely AI/ATS screening probability is high for the stated must-have requirements. Adding the exact job-language terms “FIFO stock rotation” and “temperature and hygiene checks” would improve matching further. There are no formatting or parsing problems apparent in the supplied text.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter strongly matches the two must-have requirements: completed butcher training and HACCP knowledge. It also demonstrates the main role activities of cutting, boning, trimming, portioning, customer advice, hygiene, and counter service. The tone aligns well with FreshCart’s emphasis on reliability, friendliness, hygiene, and product knowledge, particularly through the reference to the “Ask the counter” approach. The candidate’s experience is from butcher shops and a market stall rather than a supermarket, so the letter does not demonstrate experience with self-service packaging, tray sealers, supermarket labelling scales, or maintaining stocked self-service shelves; these are experience gaps rather than defects in the letter. The candidate does not hold a forklift licence, which is only a nice-to-have requirement.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the second paragraph, after “record temperature checks twice daily,” add the supported sentence: “I also rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO, with older stock placed at the front, and maintain temperature records for the cold room and display counter as part of daily hygiene controls.” This makes the letter match the advertisement’s exact “FIFO” and “temperature and hygiene checks” terminology without claiming unsupported supermarket or packaging experience.

requirements.requirement: Completed butcher training or at least 2 years at a meat counter
